environment_evidence.memory_gate: pilot observed 822MB/744MB/617MB available, below 3,204,448,256B; after stopping MSSQLSERVER/SSIS and closing apps, ~9.8-11GB available
environment_evidence.conclusion: The machine is not short of CPU or raw SQLite fsync throughput. The residual failures are timing/locking/relay instability in the LOAD harness under sustained load, plus external memory pressure when the host is shared.

diagnostic_findings: The cancel handler itself blocked ~5s while the client deadline is exactly 5s; busy_timeout=5000 leaves zero margin and the handler can legally reply after the client has timed out.
A relay telemetry/monitor failure is treated as fatal by the owner, aborting an otherwise healthy execution service; the relay wrapper also loses the underlying error code in some paths.
The stall-dump instrumentation added during diagnosis caused owner startup failure and was reverted in 393f5fbb.
No formal LOAD01 PASS is claimed; pilot pass plus partial full runs are insufficient.
flip_path: Run the fixed 10/2 matrix on a quiet host or the second machine with >=6GB free and no SQL Server/desktop contention; require zero RPC timeouts, zero relay errors, normal close, and the registered 2GiB reserve.

Or harden the harness before rerun: deadline-aware store retry below 5s, consolidate/remove redundant writer-lease transactions, latch/retry relay errors instead of aborting the owner, and make terminal catch-up wait on a durable cursor rather than a single probe.
Re-run U0 pilot after any source change, then U0/N1-N6; keep the evaluator binding to the exact producer commit and preserve the 5s/10s/2GiB thresholds.

failure.message: LOAD01 terminal market catch-up did not prove delivery

pilot_terminal_catchup_r2.observed: Even with ~6-11GB free and MSSQLSERVER/SSIS stopped, the U0 pilot terminal market catch-up took 13.578s against a 10s bound; all 20 streams had nonzero queues/receipts behind. This is a real 10s recovery performance failure, not host memory exhaustion.
